comment: Plain-English headlines + summaries per motion, generated by `python -m ingest.summarize_motions` and merged into docs/data*.json by build_dataset. Keyed by a content hash of the motion (see summarize_motions.motion_key) — NOT by motion id, which renumbers. Safe to hand-edit: a corrected entry is never overwritten unless you pass --force.

0135067145f729e9.headline: Accessory apartment exception for the Atkinson property
0135067145f729e9.summary: The commission approved an exception for an accessory dwelling unit, such as a basement or backyard apartment, on the Atkinson property.
0135067145f729e9.impact: One household is directly affected, plus perhaps its immediate neighbors. The record gives no address and does not say which rule was waived.

0165ae9da625336a.headline: Chapel and recreation development agreement
0165ae9da625336a.summary: Ahead of the site plan, the commission recommended that the council approve the development agreement for the Eagle Mountain chapel and recreation building.
0165ae9da625336a.impact: Nothing is signed until the council votes. The site plan the commission recommended the same night depends on this agreement clearing the council first.

01edf819164252d8.headline: Site plan for Lot 3 at The District
01edf819164252d8.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve the site plan for Lot 3 at The District.
01edf819164252d8.impact: The motion does not describe what would be built on the lot. People near The District should watch for the council vote, which decides whether the plan goes ahead.

02a0d558f980a190.headline: June 24 commission minutes approved
02a0d558f980a190.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its June 24, 2025 meeting.
02a0d558f980a190.impact: This makes the written record of the last meeting official. You will not notice any change.

02e2b6772876c281.headline: Chapel and recreation building site plan
02e2b6772876c281.summary: The commission backed the site plan for the Eagle Mountain chapel and recreation building on two conditions: the development agreement passes first, and the lighting plan meets city standards.
02e2b6772876c281.impact: Neighbors of the site will see no construction on the strength of this vote. The council still has to sign off, and the applicant has to bring its lighting plan into compliance.

034d9672198c8045.headline: May 26 minutes approved
034d9672198c8045.summary: The commission approved its May 26 minutes after correcting the record to list Commissioner Jensen as the alternate commissioner.
034d9672198c8045.impact: A title fix in the meeting record, made by the commission itself. Nobody outside the room feels this one.

0516c7f9b72368d5.headline: Gateway Park Phase 3 lots, street renamed
0516c7f9b72368d5.summary: The commission recommended the early layout of lots for Gateway Park Phase 3 and asked that Gateway Park Boulevard be renamed Wild Blossom Boulevard.
0516c7f9b72368d5.impact: If the council agrees, homes in this phase could face directly onto the area's larger through streets unless the developer finds room for internal roads. Anyone giving directions will need the new street name.

07c7317a1f8207e8.headline: SR-73 monument sign rules pushed to next meeting
07c7317a1f8207e8.summary: The commission delayed a decision on monument signs for businesses along SR-73 until its next meeting so staff could keep working on the proposal.
07c7317a1f8207e8.impact: Business owners on SR-73 should watch the next agenda. For now the sign rules stay as they are.

0833f445eddbb6c5.headline: Ranches Academy addition sent to council
0833f445eddbb6c5.summary: The commission recommended the City Council approve a site plan for an addition to Ranches Academy.
0833f445eddbb6c5.impact: The council has the final word on this one. The motion gives no size or timeline for the addition, so families at the school have nothing new to plan around yet.

0af5ff7ee63ab740.headline: Change to the final plat rules
0af5ff7ee63ab740.summary: The commission asked the council to change the city's code section governing final plats for subdivisions.
0af5ff7ee63ab740.impact: Surveyors and developers filing subdivision paperwork are the ones who work in this section. For everyone else it is invisible, and the council has yet to vote on it.

0b5dfc21e629ab8c.headline: Trails at Hidden Valley put on hold
0b5dfc21e629ab8c.summary: The commission tabled Trails at Hidden Valley, putting off any recommendation on it to a later meeting.
0b5dfc21e629ab8c.impact: For now, nothing has changed. The item can come back to the commission later.

0e3d44f4c724aba3.headline: February 24 minutes approved
0e3d44f4c724aba3.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its February 24, 2026 meeting.
0e3d44f4c724aba3.impact: Paperwork for the commission's own files. You will not see it.

104e1f51d74f36cf.headline: Annexation policy plan
104e1f51d74f36cf.summary: Commissioners took up the city's annexation policy plan, the document that sets which land Eagle Mountain may take in, and sent it toward the council.
104e1f51d74f36cf.impact: The minutes do not record how the vote came out. Annexation shapes the city's future boundaries, so this one is worth watching when the council picks it up.

10858ab696a61b84.headline: Spring Run Plaza Lot 1 building plan
10858ab696a61b84.summary: The commission recommended the building plan for Lot 1 of Spring Run Plaza, with no added conditions.
10858ab696a61b84.impact: This one is a recommendation, so the City Council still decides. The motion gives no detail on what will be built on the lot.

1215b675e78a6a26.headline: Cost estimate rules for subdivision work
1215b675e78a6a26.summary: The commission asked the council to update the code sections covering cost estimates for subdivision and development work.
1215b675e78a6a26.impact: The council makes the call at a later meeting. Engineers and developers pricing out required improvements would feel this; a homeowner would not.

13885e47df5c1cec.headline: New setbacks for buildings that house animals
13885e47df5c1cec.summary: The commission recommended that the council change how far buildings that house animals must sit from property lines.
13885e47df5c1cec.impact: If the council agrees, anyone building a barn, coop or similar structure would have to follow the new distances. The motion does not give the distances, and the council still has to vote.

146f0225bfdd72af.headline: July 22 minutes approved
146f0225bfdd72af.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its July 22, 2025, meeting.
146f0225bfdd72af.impact: This makes the written record of the last meeting official. You will not see it anywhere else.

15c5fc8faf557717.headline: Firefly NPA 9 Phase A master site plan
15c5fc8faf557717.summary: The commission recommended the master site plan for Firefly NPA 9 Phase A to the City Council, with staff's recommendations included.
15c5fc8faf557717.impact: This plan goes to the City Council next. Until the council acts, it changes nothing on the ground in Firefly.

1aae4c80984b33c2.headline: Parking exception for Redemption Hill
1aae4c80984b33c2.summary: The commission approved a parking exception for Redemption Hill; the motion does not say which parking rule was waived or by how much.
1aae4c80984b33c2.impact: This touches one property. Anyone parking there may notice a difference, but the record gives no details to say what it will be.

1bba5b01f6a1bc9b.headline: Rules for building on slopes
1bba5b01f6a1bc9b.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve changes to the city code covering development on sloped land.
1bba5b01f6a1bc9b.impact: If the council adopts it, people building on hillside lots would be affected. The motion does not say what the new rules require, and none of them apply until the council votes.

229dfb0f7d8382cb.headline: New sign rules for athletic fields
229dfb0f7d8382cb.summary: The commission recommended sign rules for athletic facilities: signs must attach to the fence, scoreboard or bleachers, may face in or out, and may not rise above them.
229dfb0f7d8382cb.impact: Sports leagues and sponsors hanging banners at fields would follow these limits once the council acts. People living near a field could see signs facing outward.

2731676dbb9ae016.headline: September 9 minutes approved
2731676dbb9ae016.summary: The commission signed off on the minutes from its September 9, 2025 meeting.
2731676dbb9ae016.impact: A record-keeping step for the commission's own files. No one outside the room is touched by it.

27b1405b06cfc762.headline: One Call Auto site plan forwarded
27b1405b06cfc762.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve the site plan for One Call Auto.
27b1405b06cfc762.impact: Construction cannot proceed on this recommendation alone, since the council decides. It concerns one business's property and nobody else's.

2a9aafa8c09b1d1a.headline: Change to final plat rules recommended
2a9aafa8c09b1d1a.summary: The commission recommended a change to the city code on final plats, the recorded maps that divide land into lots, and sent it to the council.
2a9aafa8c09b1d1a.impact: Developers dividing land would follow the new rules if the council adopts them. The motion does not describe what changes.

2b21399d6e3b1f9e.headline: Parkway Fields stake center sent to council
2b21399d6e3b1f9e.summary: The commission recommended the Parkway Fields stake center to the City Council and left it to the council to decide whether to allow a different building setback.
2b21399d6e3b1f9e.impact: Nothing is final until the council votes, including how far the building will sit from the property line. Neighbors of the site have the most reason to follow the council vote.

2ba6ec9036bac2f2.headline: Drive-thru lane rule changes recommended
2ba6ec9036bac2f2.summary: The commission sent the council a recommendation to amend the city code's rules for drive-thru lanes.
2ba6ec9036bac2f2.impact: Restaurants and other businesses planning a drive-thru would follow the new rules once the council adopts them. For most people this one stays out of sight.

2c0fd66a7bc21a30.headline: Taller screening plants along parking lots
2c0fd66a7bc21a30.summary: The commission backed new landscape and buffering rules, rewriting one line to require a continuous 3.5-foot-tall wall of plants to block headlights.
2c0fd66a7bc21a30.impact: Developers planting new parking areas would have to put in trees, shrubs or grasses tall enough at planting to hide headlights from neighbors. The council decides whether it becomes law.

2c69342be60e09e2.headline: Granite Credit Union's sign request denied
2c69342be60e09e2.summary: The commission refused to let Granite Credit Union break the city's sign rules, finding it knew the code and its building's visibility when it chose the site.
2c69342be60e09e2.impact: The credit union must keep its signs within the same limits every other business in the district follows. Only this one business is affected.

2d774f78f8f3bd6e.headline: Brandon Park zoning change moves to council
2d774f78f8f3bd6e.summary: The commission recommended the council approve a zoning change for Brandon Park.
2d774f78f8f3bd6e.impact: A zoning change decides what can be built on the land, so neighbors have reason to follow it. Acreage and the new zone are not in the record here, and the council still has to vote.

30d3aeee4b2653b8.headline: June 10 minutes
30d3aeee4b2653b8.summary: The commission took up approval of the minutes from its June 10, 2025 meeting; the record does not show the result.
30d3aeee4b2653b8.impact: Minutes are the official record of the last meeting. You will not feel this one.

31df220494676928.headline: Retaining wall variance denied on Wright property
31df220494676928.summary: The commission turned down a request to bypass the city's retaining wall rules, finding the lot has room for a tiered wall meeting standards.
31df220494676928.impact: The owner must build to the city's tiered wall standard rather than the wall proposed. Sloped ground on its own will not win a variance, which matters to anyone with a hillside lot.

3245531dd17f9b85.headline: Horizon development plan turned down
3245531dd17f9b85.summary: The commission denied the Horizon master development plan and preliminary plat, the first map showing how the land would be divided into lots.
3245531dd17f9b85.impact: The Horizon project can't move ahead on this version of its plan. The record doesn't say why it was denied or whether the developer can appeal or bring it back.

3250a11604a343d8.headline: December 9 minutes held for later
3250a11604a343d8.summary: The commission put off approving the minutes of its December 9, 2025 meeting.
3250a11604a343d8.impact: The record of that meeting stays unofficial for now. You will not notice the delay.

33a7550989ea99d2.headline: Mountainland development agreement
33a7550989ea99d2.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve the Mountainland development agreement, a contract setting the terms for building on a piece of land.
33a7550989ea99d2.impact: The council has the final say. The motion gives no location, size or terms, so it is not yet clear who will live near this project or what will be built.

34350f5f0478735a.headline: Item 7.A sent to council with wildlife group input
34350f5f0478735a.summary: The commission recommended Item 7.A to the council, asking that comments from the Eagle Mountain Nature and Wildlife Alliance be included.
34350f5f0478735a.impact: The record names the item only as 7.A, so its contents are not stated here. The council has the final vote and will see the wildlife group's comments alongside it.

399e2b2bae962f59.headline: August 26 minutes approved
399e2b2bae962f59.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its August 26, 2025 meeting.
399e2b2bae962f59.impact: Approving the minutes makes that meeting's written record official. It changes nothing for anyone in the city.

3a737e20aabcd93d.headline: Chapel and rec building site plan shelved
3a737e20aabcd93d.summary: The site plan for the Eagle Mountain Chapel and Recreation Building was set aside by the commission for a later meeting.
3a737e20aabcd93d.impact: The plan sits where it is until the commission picks it up again. Nobody's property or paperwork changes in the meantime.

3ad1a96a9e5e6cdd.headline: Firefly NPA 9 Phase A lot layout approved
3ad1a96a9e5e6cdd.summary: The commission approved the preliminary plat for Firefly NPA 9 Phase A, the early lot-and-street layout, with staff's recommendations attached.
3ad1a96a9e5e6cdd.impact: The developer can move this phase of Firefly toward a final plat. People living near Firefly are the ones who will see the result.

4084f8f2aae2a916.headline: August 12 commission minutes approved
4084f8f2aae2a916.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its August 12, 2025 meeting.
4084f8f2aae2a916.impact: This makes the written record of the last meeting official. You will not notice it.

40cc337c35241243.headline: September 2 minutes approved
40cc337c35241243.summary: The commission accepted the minutes of its September 2, 2025 meeting as the official record.
40cc337c35241243.impact: Housekeeping only. It changes nothing for residents.

41a4b35505ba1a47.headline: Change to preliminary plat rules recommended
41a4b35505ba1a47.summary: A matching change for preliminary plats, the early lot layouts a developer submits, also won the commission's recommendation to the council.
41a4b35505ba1a47.impact: This is for people applying to build subdivisions. Homeowners won't notice it, and the council still has to act.

41ca21da03d3e853.headline: Spring Run Plaza plat held to April 28
41ca21da03d3e853.summary: A decision on the preliminary plat for Spring Run Plaza was pushed to the commission's April 28, 2026 meeting.
41ca21da03d3e853.impact: Two more weeks before anything is decided about this project. If you want to weigh in, the item comes back at the end of the month.

4759c6887435eeb8.headline: Temporary site plan for Sweetwater Stake Center
4759c6887435eeb8.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve an 18-month temporary site plan for the Sweetwater Stake Center.
4759c6887435eeb8.impact: Nothing takes effect yet: the council makes the final call. The motion does not say what the temporary plan covers, so whatever changes it brings would last 18 months at that one site.

47b727c7fbb9e015.headline: September 23 minutes approved
47b727c7fbb9e015.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its September 23, 2025 meeting.
47b727c7fbb9e015.impact: This makes the written record of that meeting official. You will not see it anywhere.

481986547e66d9a3.headline: Change to the residential standards table
481986547e66d9a3.summary: The commission recommended that the council amend the residential standards table in the zoning code, without stating in the motion what the change alters.
481986547e66d9a3.impact: The motion does not say which standards move, so there is nothing yet to tell homeowners what they could build differently. The council decides whether it takes effect.

4a6ba78ff7890dde.headline: Transportation master plan pushed to June 24
4a6ba78ff7890dde.summary: The commission delayed a decision on the Transportation Master Plan and its Impact Fee Facilities Plan, and kept the public hearing open until June 24, 2025.
4a6ba78ff7890dde.impact: Nothing about roads or fees changed at this meeting. If you want to speak on the plan, the hearing is still open on June 24.

4ac9165d616ce233.headline: First-stage plat for Spring Run Plaza
4ac9165d616ce233.summary: Backing the site's lot layout, the commission sent the Spring Run Plaza preliminary plat to the council, conditioned on a signed agreement and the extended turn lane.
4ac9165d616ce233.impact: This is the lot layout step, and it holds until the council acts and the agreement is signed. Builders on that site are watching; nobody else needs to.

4ac9f0cb302bbc7a.headline: Noise rules for land rezoned after a project is built
4ac9f0cb302bbc7a.summary: The commission recommended a noise ordinance change: when land next to an approved project is later rezoned for quieter use, the rezoned land pays for any noise fixes.
4ac9f0cb302bbc7a.impact: If a business near you was approved under the old noise limits, rezoning your side later would not force it to quiet down. The council still has to vote.

4b782929b3b334ac.headline: Stricter screening rules for HVAC equipment
4b782929b3b334ac.summary: The commission asked the council to change the city's HVAC screening rules: allow polyethylene, drop landscaping as an option, and require screens within 6 inches of the ground.
4b782929b3b334ac.impact: Nothing changes yet, the council votes on this later. If it passes, anyone installing air conditioning equipment would have to box it in rather than hide it behind plants, and paint the connecting lines to match the wall.

506083e19942f45b.headline: July 8 minutes approved
506083e19942f45b.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its July 8, 2025 meeting.
506083e19942f45b.impact: This is record-keeping only, and nobody outside the room is touched by it.

52e4463aab2b4bf1.headline: Animal management plan standards put off
52e4463aab2b4bf1.summary: The commission pushed its review of proposed standards for alternative animal management plans to its July 8, 2025 meeting.
52e4463aab2b4bf1.impact: No decision was made, so the current rules still apply. Anyone following this item should watch the July 8 agenda.

530b715eb4d15083.headline: Culinary water impact fee plan sent to council
530b715eb4d15083.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt the culinary water impact fee facility plan, which lists the drinking water projects new growth must help pay for.
530b715eb4d15083.impact: This is still only advice to the council, which decides later. The plan mostly matters to developers, since it underpins the water fee charged on new construction.

5566d8c4c622ae28.headline: Item 7C sent to the council with support
5566d8c4c622ae28.summary: The commission recommended council approval of Item 7C. The motion as recorded gives no description of the item.
5566d8c4c622ae28.impact: Nothing takes effect from this vote. What Item 7C covers, and whom it reaches, is not stated in the motion.

5819f5e0ab0f8dcf.headline: January 13 minutes fixed and approved
5819f5e0ab0f8dcf.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its January 13, 2026 meeting after correcting who led the Pledge of Allegiance, from Commissioner Allen to Commissioner Hess.
5819f5e0ab0f8dcf.impact: A one-line correction to the record. It changes nothing for anyone outside the room.

5ba14bd0fa5a3505.headline: June 23 minutes approved
5ba14bd0fa5a3505.summary: The commission signed off on the minutes of its June 23, 2026 meeting.
5ba14bd0fa5a3505.impact: This is the housekeeping that makes the written record of that meeting official. You will not feel it anywhere.

5cf3889fea1cabc2.headline: Update to diagrams in the subdivision code
5cf3889fea1cabc2.summary: The commission recommended amending the diagrams section of the city's subdivision code, chapter 16.35.140.
5cf3889fea1cabc2.impact: Engineers and developers drawing up new subdivisions are the ones who use these diagrams. A homeowner is unlikely to notice, and the council still has to vote on it.

5e42a49a49b6fe84.headline: Horizon Master Community held for new notice
5e42a49a49b6fe84.summary: The commission set aside the Horizon Master Community until the city gives fresh public notice of it as a development agreement.
5e42a49a49b6fe84.impact: The project goes nowhere for now. A new notice means the public gets another formal chance to hear about it before anyone votes.

5eedad57e3615eaf.headline: City fee schedule update sent to council
5eedad57e3615eaf.summary: The commission recommended the council adopt changes to the city's consolidated fee schedule, except the illegal dumping section, which it held for its next meeting.
5eedad57e3615eaf.impact: The motion lists no fee amounts, so what you might pay is not in the record. The council decides, and the dumping section returns to the commission first.

5f319cb18adac4a8.headline: Stadion LLC development agreement sent to council
5f319cb18adac4a8.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve a development agreement with Stadion LLC.
5f319cb18adac4a8.impact: Nothing is binding yet; the council makes the final call. The motion gives no detail on what Stadion plans to build or where.

608e7ddb9491a388.headline: October 28 minutes approved
608e7ddb9491a388.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its October 28, 2025 meeting.
608e7ddb9491a388.impact: This makes the commission's record of that meeting official. You will not notice it.

6196574fec3fbfb7.headline: March minutes fixed and approved
6196574fec3fbfb7.summary: The commission approved its March 24, 2026 minutes after correcting the record to show Commissioner Hess led the Pledge of Allegiance.
6196574fec3fbfb7.impact: Housekeeping that makes the last meeting's record official. Nobody outside the meeting room feels it.

6288877d621c994b.headline: Energy overlay zone, minus water-cooled gas plants
6288877d621c994b.summary: The commission recommended that the council adopt Chapter 17.64, the Alternative Energy Overlay Zone, with water-cooled natural gas power plants excluded from it.
6288877d621c994b.impact: The council has the final vote. If it agrees, no water-cooled natural gas power plant could be built under this overlay, wherever the overlay is applied.

62df6414f3df5e85.headline: Williams development agreement sent to council
62df6414f3df5e85.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve the Williams Development Agreement.
62df6414f3df5e85.impact: Nothing takes effect yet: the council makes the final call later. The motion does not say where the land is or what would be built there.

64c6660e8ea69c85.headline: November 25 minutes
64c6660e8ea69c85.summary: The commission took up a motion to approve the minutes of its November 25, 2025 meeting, and the record doesn't show how the vote went.
64c6660e8ea69c85.impact: Minutes are the commission's own record of an earlier meeting. Nobody outside the room is affected.

6508d7f295d4ff28.headline: Angel's Landing lot split approved
6508d7f295d4ff28.summary: The commission approved the Angel's Landing lot split, dividing the property into separate lots; the motion records neither the acreage nor how many lots result.
6508d7f295d4ff28.impact: This one the commission settled itself, with no council vote to follow. It redraws lot lines at Angel's Landing and touches the owner and immediate neighbors, not the wider city.

650bbab12bfbd9fc.headline: Sewer master plan and impact fee plan sent to council
650bbab12bfbd9fc.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt a wastewater master plan and the facility plan used to set sewer impact fees on new development.
650bbab12bfbd9fc.impact: Nothing takes effect yet; the council has the final vote. If adopted, these plans guide future sewer projects and what builders of new homes pay toward them.

66ace69061284f4a.headline: Directional signs for data centers
66ace69061284f4a.summary: The commission recommended a code change on directional signs for data centers, and added a line so the rule also covers the Alternate Energy Overlay Zone.
66ace69061284f4a.impact: Nothing changes until the City Council votes. If it passes, the rule applies to data center sites and to land in that energy overlay zone, not to homeowners.

675e0a11f004e415.headline: July 14 minutes fixed and approved
675e0a11f004e415.summary: The commission approved its July 14 minutes after correcting Commissioner Hess's recorded vote from yes to abstain.
675e0a11f004e415.impact: The official record now shows how Commissioner Hess voted that night. Beyond that file, nobody's day changes.

67cab1f229d9f8df.headline: Seasonal political sign rules
67cab1f229d9f8df.summary: Commissioners backed changes to the city's rules on seasonal political signs, with one clerical error corrected before it moves to the council.
67cab1f229d9f8df.impact: If the council agrees, the rules for putting campaign signs on your property around an election would change. Nothing is in force yet.

6a9e1cd424c21947.headline: July 28 minutes approved with a correction
6a9e1cd424c21947.summary: The commission approved its July 28, 2026 minutes after fixing the record to show Commissioner Hess made the motion on Item 7.A.
6a9e1cd424c21947.impact: A correction to the written record of a past meeting. It touches the file the city keeps and nothing you will encounter.

6adae8ba70d2673b.headline: Change to the city's table of allowed land uses
6adae8ba70d2673b.summary: The commission recommended a change to the city code's land use table, which lists the uses allowed in each zone.
6adae8ba70d2673b.impact: The record does not name the uses being added, removed or moved. Whatever the change is, it waits on a City Council vote before it applies to any property.

6b0263cd701a145d.headline: March 10 minutes approved
6b0263cd701a145d.summary: The commission signed off on the written record of its March 10, 2026 meeting.
6b0263cd701a145d.impact: Bookkeeping that makes the last meeting's record official. Nothing here reaches a resident.

6b981f532a976e6b.headline: Animal, ADU and home business rules held over
6b981f532a976e6b.summary: The commission tabled a code change on animals, exceptions, public hearings and appeals until its next meeting so staff could revisit tables for animals, ADUs and home businesses.
6b981f532a976e6b.impact: Nothing changed. If you keep animals, rent out an accessory apartment or run a business from home, watch for this item when it returns.

6e15c1dafe5c3d89.headline: Meritage Homes privacy screening agreement
6e15c1dafe5c3d89.summary: The commission recommended a development agreement with Meritage Homes covering privacy screening, and passed it to the City Council for a final vote.
6e15c1dafe5c3d89.impact: If the council agrees, the deal sets privacy screening terms for a Meritage Homes project. The record does not say which neighborhood or what kind of screening.

71d0a6bba65ab2c6.headline: Elementary school 133 plans wait for zoning change
71d0a6bba65ab2c6.summary: The commission tabled the preliminary plat and site plan for ASD Elementary 133 until the applicant returns with a zoning change request.
71d0a6bba65ab2c6.impact: Plans for this school are paused. Expect the item back once a zoning change is filed, and not before.

7234a264346bab4e.headline: Variance denied for Pony Express Business Park
7234a264346bab4e.summary: The commission refused to waive the wash setback, retaining wall and drive-through circulation rules for the Pony Express Business Park site.
7234a264346bab4e.impact: Whoever builds there has to meet the standard setback, wall and drive-through rules or come back with a redesign. The commission found the lot still holds room for a workable commercial building. Nothing changes for anyone who does not build on that property.

72782bcbd098817f.headline: Water plan update sent to council
72782bcbd098817f.summary: The commission recommended changes to the city's water use and preservation plan, asking for new population figures and an account of water developers bring in.
72782bcbd098817f.impact: The plan guides how the city pipes water to new growth and what impact fees pay for, so a weak plan reaches every tap. The council decides whether to adopt it.

738bb7b5e19d8365.headline: Flagship development agreement sent to council
738bb7b5e19d8365.summary: The commission asked the City Council to approve a development agreement for Flagship, the terms of which the motion does not spell out.
738bb7b5e19d8365.impact: Nothing is settled yet: the council takes the final vote. The record here gives no location, acreage or unit count, so what it would build is not something this motion tells you.

7442cacfb274e6af.headline: Fee schedule sent to council with two fixes
7442cacfb274e6af.summary: The commission backed the city's consolidated fee schedule, asking that a 180-day deposit-holding line be struck and an unfinished footnote be completed.
7442cacfb274e6af.impact: The fee schedule sets what you pay the city for permits and inspections. Nothing changes yet: the council takes the final vote, and these two edits are cleanup rather than new charges.

744648d139f8de6e.headline: John Hancock Charter School plan put on hold
744648d139f8de6e.summary: The commission tabled a second look at the master site plan for John Hancock Charter School, and the record gives no date to bring it back.
744648d139f8de6e.impact: Nothing about the school changes for now. Families there will see no difference until the plan returns to the commission.

752bd2c0b420b9af.headline: QTS SCL 2 zoning change backed
752bd2c0b420b9af.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve a zoning change for the property known as QTS SCL 2.
752bd2c0b420b9af.impact: The council has the final vote, so this land's zoning stays as it is for now. The motion gives no acreage, location or planned use.

76988ac964a87365.headline: Cell tower at Available Storage
76988ac964a87365.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve the site plan for a Meta cell tower at Available Storage.
76988ac964a87365.impact: Nothing is built on this vote. The City Council makes the final call on the tower, and neighbors of the storage site have the most at stake.

786464d258756eb8.headline: Commission opposes fence rule change
786464d258756eb8.summary: The commission advised the City Council to reject a proposed amendment to the city's fence code.
786464d258756eb8.impact: Your fence rules stay as they are for now. The council makes the final call and does not have to follow this advice. The motion does not say what the change would have done.

7b0e8d66b37f817f.headline: Senior housing overlay zone recommended
7b0e8d66b37f817f.summary: The commission backed a new senior housing overlay zone, with accessory dwelling units barred inside it and five rural zones cut off from density bonuses.
7b0e8d66b37f817f.impact: If the council agrees, builders could add senior housing at higher density in some areas, though not in the RA1, RA2, RD1, RD2 or FR zones. Renting out a basement apartment would be off limits in these developments.

7be7088f3f0a9737.headline: Pool amenity for Hidden Hollow
7be7088f3f0a9737.summary: The commission recommended the Hidden Hollow pool amenity to the City Council and asked that the clubhouse also get an added amenity.
7be7088f3f0a9737.impact: This mainly concerns people who live or will live in Hidden Hollow. The council still has to vote, and the motion doesn't say what the clubhouse addition would be.

7f6aa32268bdb965.headline: Richard's animal management plan delayed
7f6aa32268bdb965.summary: The commission delayed a decision on Richard's animal management plan until its July 8, 2025 meeting.
7f6aa32268bdb965.impact: This is one property owner's request. It waits two weeks, and neighbors have nothing new to react to yet.

807ed236563569d2.headline: Transportation plan and road impact fees
807ed236563569d2.summary: The commission recommended the council adopt the city's transportation master plan and the impact fee facilities plan that goes with it, with changes noted by David Salazar.
807ed236563569d2.impact: Impact fees are what builders pay toward new roads, so this plan sits behind those fee amounts. The council sets both, and until it votes, nothing changes for drivers or homebuyers.

84b630396747584e.headline: Rewrite of who does what in the zoning code
84b630396747584e.summary: The commission recommended the council adopt changes to city code chapter 17.15, which sets out roles and duties, and asked for a look at how other cities handle appointments.
84b630396747584e.impact: Nothing changes until the council votes. The record does not say whose roles shift, so it is unclear whether anyone outside city hall would notice.

854b16cb37f909fe.headline: Moderate income housing section of the general plan
854b16cb37f909fe.summary: The commission recommended the council amend the moderate income housing section of the city's general plan, the long-range document that guides growth.
854b16cb37f909fe.impact: The motion does not say what the amendment changes. It takes effect only if the council approves it, and it changes no rule on your property by itself.

8a5ce932bfd0fbf8.headline: Citywide parks, trails and open space plan
8a5ce932bfd0fbf8.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt a master plan for the city's parks, trails and open space.
8a5ce932bfd0fbf8.impact: Nothing changes yet: the council makes the decision. The motion does not say what the plan contains, so it gives no detail on which parks or trails it covers.

8b064be18bca8d06.headline: February 10 minutes approved
8b064be18bca8d06.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its February 10, 2026 meeting after fixing a wrong date in the page footer.
8b064be18bca8d06.impact: Fixing a typo in the meeting record changes nothing for anyone outside the commission.

8b16e6be1b20993a.headline: Trails at Hidden Valley plan sent on with conditions
8b16e6be1b20993a.summary: The commission recommended changes to the Lower Hidden Valley master development plan for Trails at Hidden Valley, asking for a closer look at a wildlife corridor and ridgeline protection.
8b16e6be1b20993a.impact: If you live near Hidden Valley, watch the council vote. The commission wants the plats split into sections, phases one and two possibly swapped, and an answer on who fences the wildlife corridor.

8b78ccef9861e3d6.headline: Rezone parcels in White Hills
8b78ccef9861e3d6.summary: The commission recommended the White Hills zoning change with staff's condition, moving White Hills County Estates A parcels to RA2 and J & J Ranches to agriculture.
8b78ccef9861e3d6.impact: If you own property in White Hills County Estates A or J & J Ranches, this changes your zoning label. Nothing takes effect until the City Council votes.

8ba2a59c9b41cc93.headline: Pony Express Medical plans sent to council
8ba2a59c9b41cc93.summary: The commission recommended the council approve Pony Express Medical on two conditions: the landscape plan corrections get made, and the plans identify the building's exterior finishes.
8ba2a59c9b41cc93.impact: The City Council has the final say. Until it votes, the project has no green light.

8e1f5b66a037e1b3.headline: Scenic Mountain zoning change recommended
8e1f5b66a037e1b3.summary: The commission asked the City Council to approve the Scenic Mountain rezone; the motion names no acreage, location, or new zoning district.
8e1f5b66a037e1b3.impact: Land use does not change until the council votes. Residents who care what gets built there should follow the item to that meeting.

8f65c672f58b85b7.headline: Stadion development deal change sent to council
8f65c672f58b85b7.summary: The commission backed a first amendment to the Stadion development agreement and passed it to the City Council for the final vote.
8f65c672f58b85b7.impact: Nothing changes on the ground from this vote. The council takes it up later and can decide otherwise.

91b547edb2d8eb94.headline: June 9 minutes approved
91b547edb2d8eb94.summary: The commission approved the written record of its June 9, 2026 meeting.
91b547edb2d8eb94.impact: Housekeeping for the clerk's file, and nothing more.

9450bb25439878cb.headline: Pinnacles zoning change sent to the council
9450bb25439878cb.summary: The commission asked the City Council to approve the Pinnacles zoning change and an amendment to the master development plan agreement for the site.
9450bb25439878cb.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. The council holds the final vote and can decide otherwise, so if you live near the Pinnacles site, that is the meeting to watch.

971b2c6bf1537726.headline: Brylee Farms Phase B agreement change
971b2c6bf1537726.summary: The commission recommended the second amendment to the development agreement for Phase B of Brylee Farms, the contract setting what the developer may build there.
971b2c6bf1537726.impact: The council makes the final call. The motion does not say what the amendment changes, so its effect on the neighborhood cannot be told from this record.

9c4f761d2be02715.headline: Hidden Hollow clubhouse amenity swap opposed
9c4f761d2be02715.summary: The commission recommended that the council deny a minor site plan to swap the clubhouse amenity in Hidden Hollow.
9c4f761d2be02715.impact: This is a recommendation, and the council makes the final call. The record does not say what amenity would have been swapped or why the commission opposed it.

a045dc56e11b8812.headline: Master site plan rules, result unrecorded
a045dc56e11b8812.summary: Commissioners took up a change to the city code section on master site plans and moved to recommend it to the council; the minutes do not record the result.
a045dc56e11b8812.impact: Master site plans are a developer's step, not yours. With no result written down, it is not clear this recommendation ever reached the council at all.

a1ec24b85257f914.headline: Changes to the city fee schedule sent to council
a1ec24b85257f914.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council amend the city's consolidated fee schedule, the single list of what the city charges for its services and permits.
a1ec24b85257f914.impact: Nothing changes yet: the council makes the final call. The motion does not say which fees would move or by how much, so whether you would pay more is not stated.

a25fbbcdb9b2ac23.headline: Item 7D sent to the council with support
a25fbbcdb9b2ac23.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve Item 7D. The motion does not name what the item was.
a25fbbcdb9b2ac23.impact: The record here is too thin to say who this touches. The council makes the final call later.

a3fa2d17ca43b621.headline: Earlier minutes approved
a3fa2d17ca43b621.summary: The commission approved the minutes of an earlier meeting, though the record does not say which one.
a3fa2d17ca43b621.impact: Approving minutes makes the written record of a past meeting official. You will not see any effect from it.

a4d1f8bf2a217acf.headline: September minutes held for a later meeting
a4d1f8bf2a217acf.summary: The commission postponed approving the minutes from its September 2 special meeting and its September 9 regular meeting.
a4d1f8bf2a217acf.impact: The official record of those two meetings waits a little longer. Residents will not notice.

a5c7d606433bf5e9.headline: John Hancock Charter School campus plan
a5c7d606433bf5e9.summary: The commission recommended the City Council approve a master site plan for John Hancock Charter School, on condition the project follows the approved plans.
a5c7d606433bf5e9.impact: The council still has to vote before anything is built. Families with children at the school, and neighbors nearby, have the most reason to follow it.

a8fdf2f2589736e7.headline: Revocable permits for alternative animal plans
a8fdf2f2589736e7.summary: The commission recommended the council adopt rules on alternative animal management plans and other zoning provisions, with the commission, not staff, able to revoke a plan.
a8fdf2f2589736e7.impact: If you keep animals under an alternative plan, the commission would decide whether you lose it, not the planning director or code enforcement officer. Nothing changes until the council votes.

aa75b5bc3cb74488.headline: Drive-through and parking garage rules advance
aa75b5bc3cb74488.summary: City code covering drive-throughs and structured parking would be rewritten under an amendment the commission sent to the council unchanged.
aa75b5bc3cb74488.impact: Anyone designing a drive-through restaurant or a parking structure would build to the new standards. The council has not voted, and the motion does not describe what the standards say.

aae3147029fe0f6b.headline: Change the rules for public notice of land-use items
aae3147029fe0f6b.summary: The commission recommended an ordinance changing the notice requirements in three chapters of city code, 16.05, 16.55 and 17.05.
aae3147029fe0f6b.impact: These rules govern how people hear about land-use proposals. The record does not say what changes, and the council still has to adopt it.

ab39f4189d0b13ea.headline: Changes to Projects 19 and 128 proposed
ab39f4189d0b13ea.summary: The commission weighed recommending Item 7.A with Project 19 connected to Airport Road, Project 128 removed, and the wildlife group's comments included.
ab39f4189d0b13ea.impact: This version did not go forward to the council in this form. Whatever Projects 19 and 128 are, this motion left them unchanged.

ad17442786c1f6db.headline: November 12 minutes approved with two fixes
ad17442786c1f6db.summary: The commission approved its November 12, 2025 minutes after correcting the policy session start time and recording Commissioner Fox as excused, not voting no, on Item 7.A.
ad17442786c1f6db.impact: This fixes the commission's own record. You will not notice it.

b34adc563576f11a.headline: Chapel development agreement put on hold
b34adc563576f11a.summary: The commission postponed the development agreement for the Eagle Mountain Chapel and Recreation Building without acting on it.
b34adc563576f11a.impact: No decision was reached about the chapel project. The motion sets no return date, so the record does not say when the item comes back.

b497d0ccb0652412.headline: Spring Run Plaza Lot 2 building plan
b497d0ccb0652412.summary: The commission recommended the plan for Lot 2 of Spring Run Plaza, on condition that at least 60% of the east wall is faced in high-quality natural material.
b497d0ccb0652412.impact: The council has the final vote. If it agrees, the building's east side will be mostly natural material, and the owners must file a shared parking and upkeep agreement with city staff.

b6da1825bc39415e.headline: Lot map change at Rush Creek Industrial
b6da1825bc39415e.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve an amendment to the recorded lot map for the first plat of Rush Creek Industrial, Phase A.
b6da1825bc39415e.impact: This redraws paperwork for an industrial area and goes to the council next. Unless you own land there, you will not see it.

b890f9e871e82254.headline: Meritage Homes development put off to October 14
b890f9e871e82254.summary: The commission delayed a decision on the Meritage Homes development until its October 14, 2025 meeting.
b890f9e871e82254.impact: Nothing about the project moves forward yet. Anyone following it should watch the October 14 agenda.

b8a0a895f759c17a.headline: Overland Village 2 Phase B layout approved
b8a0a895f759c17a.summary: The commission approved the preliminary layout for Overland Village 2 Phase B, on condition that street names are corrected and storm drain inlets are moved.
b8a0a895f759c17a.impact: Builders can move on to the next round of plans for this phase. Neighbors near Overland Village may see construction once those plans clear.

b946be75325e5cf9.headline: Firefly NPA 6 phase approved
b946be75325e5cf9.summary: Firefly's NPA 6 phase won the commission's approval, on condition that its screening wall meets city code and the project's agreement.
b946be75325e5cf9.impact: The builder has to put up a screening wall that meets code. The record gives no unit count, acreage or location for this phase.

bc77b3b508bda7c7.headline: Allow 1 to 2 vehicles or RVs owned by others on a property
bc77b3b508bda7c7.summary: The commission recommended approval of Item 7B, adding that 1 to 2 vehicles or RVs not titled to the owner may be parked on the property if all other requirements are met.
bc77b3b508bda7c7.impact: This could matter if you park a friend's or relative's RV or car on land covered by this item. It is not in force: the City Council decides.

bde2ed4380388812.headline: Parking lots must sit near the uses they serve
bde2ed4380388812.summary: The commission recommended rules requiring parking lots to be close to the buildings they serve, plus standards for businesses that share parking.
bde2ed4380388812.impact: Developers and business owners would design lots around these rules if the council adopts them. Shoppers might notice closer parking at future projects, but nothing is in force yet.

be7d86ef4a9fa047.headline: Hansen retaining wall variance
be7d86ef4a9fa047.summary: The commission took up a motion to let the Hansen property keep a fence and retaining wall that breaks city rules, citing problems created by a neighbor.
be7d86ef4a9fa047.impact: The record does not show how the vote came out. Either way, it concerns one homeowner's wall, and the motion itself says the general public is not affected.

c476a124bbe8455f.headline: April 14 minutes approved
c476a124bbe8455f.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its April 14 meeting.
c476a124bbe8455f.impact: Housekeeping for the record: it makes the account of that meeting official. Nothing here reaches your street.

c48401903995621a.headline: Rewrite of the site plan rules in city code
c48401903995621a.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt changes to the city's site plan rules in chapter 17 of the municipal code.
c48401903995621a.impact: Developers and builders who file site plans would work under the revised rules if the council adopts them. The motion does not describe the changes.

c48c4ecc69aa4a77.headline: Commission minutes approved
c48c4ecc69aa4a77.summary: The commission approved the minutes of an earlier meeting; the record does not say which one.
c48c4ecc69aa4a77.impact: This makes the commission's written record official. You will not notice it.

c6cd7a0ae88d57d9.headline: New planned land use for Steeplechase South
c6cd7a0ae88d57d9.summary: The commission recommended changing the city's long-range land use map for the area known as Steeplechase South.
c6cd7a0ae88d57d9.impact: This map guides what kind of building the city will later allow there. The motion does not say what the new designation is, and the council makes the final call.

cc6f9eca91969a5b.headline: Wildfire-zone map sent to the council
cc6f9eca91969a5b.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt a code change to the Wildland Urban Interface Area Map, which marks where homes border open wildland.
cc6f9eca91969a5b.impact: Nothing changes until the council votes. If it adopts the map, the map decides which properties fall inside the wildfire zone, though the motion does not say what rules apply there.

cd80bf0a6eed17a0.headline: Spring Run Plaza development plan and zoning change
cd80bf0a6eed17a0.summary: The commission recommended the Spring Run Plaza master development plan and zoning change, with the land under roads A and B zoned as agriculture.
cd80bf0a6eed17a0.impact: This sets the outline for how Spring Run Plaza can be built. The City Council makes the final call, so nothing is built on the strength of this vote.

cd818244ab15fbb3.headline: Water and sewer master plans sent to council
cd818244ab15fbb3.summary: The commission recommended the City Council adopt master plans and impact fee facilities plans for the city's drinking water system and its sewer system.
cd818244ab15fbb3.impact: These plans guide how water and sewer lines grow and what builders may be charged to pay for that growth. Nothing takes effect until the council votes.

ce982f6d0ed61450.headline: Animal and appeals code changes put off to July 22
ce982f6d0ed61450.summary: The commission delayed until its July 22, 2025 meeting a decision on code changes covering animals, exceptions, public hearings and appeals.
ce982f6d0ed61450.impact: The current rules stay as they are for now. The record does not say what the proposed changes would do.

ceda0b9679343031.headline: October 14 minutes approved
ceda0b9679343031.summary: Minutes from the commission's October 14, 2025 meeting got the commission's approval.
ceda0b9679343031.impact: Housekeeping for the commission's own records. Nobody outside the room is touched by it.

d04381571c08322f.headline: Overland development deal advanced, lighting flagged
d04381571c08322f.summary: The commission recommended the Overland Master Development Agreement to the City Council and asked that its lighting requirements be brought closer to city code.
d04381571c08322f.impact: The agreement sets the ground rules for building out Overland, and the council still has to approve it. Neighbors may care how the outdoor lighting question gets settled.

d3013fc74ef13c84.headline: August 11 minutes approved with a fix
d3013fc74ef13c84.summary: The commission approved its August 11 minutes after correcting one line to record three abstentions, not two, on an earlier vote.
d3013fc74ef13c84.impact: A clerical fix to the commission's own records. Residents will not notice it.

d420a76af46588dc.headline: Brylee Townhomes agreement change backed
d420a76af46588dc.summary: A first amendment to the Brylee Townhomes development agreement won the commission's support, with the decision left to the City Council.
d420a76af46588dc.impact: The council has the last word here, so the amendment is not in force. Neighbors of the townhome site will see no change from this step.

d4a6cc9a24193ea3.headline: Pinnacles rezoning sent to the council
d4a6cc9a24193ea3.summary: The commission asked the City Council to approve a zoning change for the Pinnacles property, without recording the acreage or the new zone in the motion.
d4a6cc9a24193ea3.impact: Nothing about the site changes yet: the council votes later and can decide otherwise. If you live near Pinnacles, that council meeting is the one to watch.

d521ded6e0063127.headline: Triumph development agreement change
d521ded6e0063127.summary: The commission recommended a second amendment to the Triumph master development agreement, which sets the terms for that development.
d521ded6e0063127.impact: The record does not say what the amendment changes. Neighbors of the Triumph project are the ones with a reason to follow it to the council.

d52395b3fa9c3fe6.headline: Backyard recreation buildings
d52395b3fa9c3fe6.summary: Over one commissioner's objection, the commission recommended a new code section on accessory recreation buildings.
d52395b3fa9c3fe6.impact: This governs what you may build on your own lot alongside your house, such as a detached recreation structure. The council has the final say.

d909ead1ce6fee59.headline: May 12 minutes approved
d909ead1ce6fee59.summary: The commission signed off on the written record of its May 12, 2026 meeting.
d909ead1ce6fee59.impact: This one lives in the clerk's files. It makes the record of the last meeting official and asks nothing of you.

dab969c0b102fea0.headline: December 9 minutes approved
dab969c0b102fea0.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its December 9 meeting; the recorded motion lists the year as 2026.
dab969c0b102fea0.impact: This step files the earlier meeting into the official record. You will not notice it.

db6148794f73a44f.headline: Brylee Commercial Lot 3 site plan backed
db6148794f73a44f.summary: The commission recommended the council approve the site plan for Lot 3 of Brylee Commercial and attached no conditions.
db6148794f73a44f.impact: The record doesn't say what would be built on the lot. The council votes next.

dd1ac09a06d9b40a.headline: Firefly townhome site plan sent to council
dd1ac09a06d9b40a.summary: The commission recommended the council approve the site plan for Plat 4 townhomes in Firefly NPA 8 Phase B, with one condition from the staff report.
dd1ac09a06d9b40a.impact: No townhomes are approved yet. That vote belongs to the council, and the motion gives no unit count.

dd69ca3b471c210a.headline: Extend the annexation map's Area 1 to Utah Lake
dd69ca3b471c210a.summary: The commission recommended amending the general plan's annexation policy declaration so that Area 1 reaches Utah Lake.
dd69ca3b471c210a.impact: The policy marks land the city might consider taking in later. It does not annex any land itself, and the City Council has not yet voted on the change.

e0bf75b4109ae2da.headline: Change to the preliminary plat rules
e0bf75b4109ae2da.summary: Commissioners also sent up a change to the code section on preliminary plats, the earlier stage of the same subdivision review.
e0bf75b4109ae2da.impact: Another one aimed at the people who file subdivision plans. Nothing here reaches your street, and the council decides whether the wording changes at all.

e56dcad788eb80cc.headline: New rules for keeping animals on home lots
e56dcad788eb80cc.summary: The commission recommended that the council rewrite the city's animal-keeping rules, add standards for alternative animal management plans, bar ostriches and emus on quarter- to half-acre lots, and rename buffalo to bison.
e56dcad788eb80cc.impact: If the council adopts this, owners of quarter- to half-acre lots could not keep ostriches or emus. Nothing changes until the council votes.

e589549960cacbe2.headline: New construction standards for retaining walls
e589549960cacbe2.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt changes to the city's construction standards for retaining walls; the motion does not say what the changes are.
e589549960cacbe2.impact: Nothing changes until the council votes. Once adopted, the new rules would apply to anyone building a retaining wall, and the record here does not spell out what they require.

e96bc40b9c7c5462.headline: Concept plan rules put off to May
e96bc40b9c7c5462.summary: The commission delayed a decision on the city's concept plan rules until its May 12 meeting.
e96bc40b9c7c5462.impact: The existing rules stay in place until then. Only people filing concept plans have a reason to follow this one.

e972832d1dc4f1e5.headline: New rules for how buildings must look
e972832d1dc4f1e5.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt changes, revised during the meeting, to the city code's architectural standards for buildings.
e972832d1dc4f1e5.impact: None of this is in force yet. If the council adopts it, anyone designing a new building will work to the revised standards. The motion does not say what the changes are.

ee8971b0fdf90ad4.headline: Revised lot layout for Marketplace 4
ee8971b0fdf90ad4.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve an amended preliminary plat for Marketplace 4, with minor map corrections to be made before the final plat.
ee8971b0fdf90ad4.impact: This is a draft of how the land in Marketplace 4 is divided, and the council still has to approve it. The motion does not say what changed from the earlier version.

f055d9da3564f753.headline: New fee for site plan changes
f055d9da3564f753.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council add a fee for site plan amendments to the city's consolidated fee schedule.
f055d9da3564f753.impact: Developers and businesses that revise approved site plans would pay it, but the motion gives no amount. Homeowners would not see it, and the council still has to approve it.

f1f74eeb0b08c5b9.headline: Setback rules along the wildlife interface boundary
f1f74eeb0b08c5b9.summary: The commission backed a code change moving the setback from the rear lot line to the wildlife urban interface boundary, and applying it to homes and outbuildings.
f1f74eeb0b08c5b9.impact: Owners whose lots touch that boundary would measure the setback from the boundary, not the back property line, and outbuildings would count too. The council has the final say.

f267e1c58e8edaf4.headline: Fixes to the city's fence rules
f267e1c58e8edaf4.summary: The commission sent the City Council a recommendation to approve a set of fixes to the city's fence code.
f267e1c58e8edaf4.impact: Homeowners planning a fence may eventually face different rules. The motion doesn't say what changes, and none of it takes effect unless the council adopts it.

f38cf39e9a44c447.headline: Pacific Springs development agreement
f38cf39e9a44c447.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve the development agreement for Pacific Springs.
f38cf39e9a44c447.impact: The council has the final vote and can still reject the agreement. The motion gives no acreage, home count or location, so the record doesn't say who would be affected or how.

f40bdad2faef43bf.headline: Spring Run Plaza development deal sent to council
f40bdad2faef43bf.summary: The commission recommended the Spring Run Plaza master development agreement, asking that the right turn lane be extended to the service drive.
f40bdad2faef43bf.impact: Nothing is built on this yet: the council votes later. Neighbors of the site and drivers turning in are the ones who would notice, with a longer turn lane feeding the plaza's service drive.

f5cdc45b2d1565de.headline: Eagle Quest development agreement amendment
f5cdc45b2d1565de.summary: The commission asked the council to approve a second amendment to the Eagle Quest master development agreement.
f5cdc45b2d1565de.impact: Master development agreements set the terms a builder must follow on a large project. The record here gives no detail on what the amendment changes, and the council has not voted on it.

f60dbe9d549ac78a.headline: Property frontage rules sent to council
f60dbe9d549ac78a.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt changes to how the city's land-use code defines and controls property frontage.
f60dbe9d549ac78a.impact: Nothing changes yet, because the council makes the final call. The record does not say what the new frontage rules are, so it is unclear whose lots they would touch.

fa191c13bd6b5da7.headline: August 25 minutes approved
fa191c13bd6b5da7.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its August 25, 2026 meeting.
fa191c13bd6b5da7.impact: Approving the minutes makes the written record of the last meeting official. You will not notice any change.

fd8bd71e7fc88723.headline: 2026 meeting calendar set
fd8bd71e7fc88723.summary: The commission adopted its 2026 meeting schedule and added one meeting on November 24, 2026.
fd8bd71e7fc88723.impact: If you follow land-use hearings, this tells you when the commission will meet next year. Beyond that, it doesn't touch anyone.

fe2baf437c027acc.headline: Barbed wire fence rules, numbering fixed
fe2baf437c027acc.summary: Commissioners sent the council a change to the barbed wire fencing rules, correcting the numbering so chain link fencing around industrial properties keeps its own subsection.
fe2baf437c027acc.impact: Fence rules stay as they are until the council acts. The correction matters most to industrial property owners and to anyone reading the code to work out which fence is allowed where.

fe6aa19ece98cb98.headline: Harmony development agreement, sections 7 and 8
fe6aa19ece98cb98.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council approve sections 7 and 8 of the Harmony development agreement.
fe6aa19ece98cb98.impact: The motion does not say what those sections cover. The council has the final vote, so nothing changes for Harmony residents or builders until it acts.

febde6f8ea1fb448.headline: Interconnectivity code change limited to five zones
febde6f8ea1fb448.summary: The commission recommended that the council adopt an interconnectivity amendment to city code, on condition that it apply to the CN, CC, CR, MEC and OP zones.
febde6f8ea1fb448.impact: Nothing changes until the council votes. The record names the five zones the rule would cover but does not say what it would require of them.
